rounds.text: The business is scaling impressively, evidenced by trailing twelve-month sales growth of 19% [E17] and a 30% surge in compounded profit growth over the same period [E21], complemented by a rules-based screen score of 96 out of 100 signaling high confidence [E64]. Furthermore, operational efficiency is strengthening as debtor days have dropped from 64.8 to 45.5 days [E59] and overall working capital requirements have contracted from 77.3 to 60.2 days [E60], all while maintaining a conservatively financed balance sheet with a debt-to-equity ratio of just 0.17x [E37]. Conceded: [E61].

Aries Agro carries substantial downside risks driven by historical and structural earnings quality concerns, underlined by a median return on equity over 10 years of just 8% and a low return on equity of 11.0% over the last 3 years [E26, E61]. The financial profile is encumbered by significant contingent liabilities totaling Rs. 167 Cr, alongside rising borrowings which increased to Rs. 56 Cr in March 2026 from Rs. 49 Cr a year earlier, coupled with a high cost of borrowing [E39, E62, E63]. Operating margins demonstrate an inconsistent trend over the last two years on both yearly and quarterly bases [E32, E33], while the equity exhibits extreme volatility of 56.8% and a severe worst peak-to-trough historical drawdown of -89.8% [E53, E54]. Conceded: the company displays a low debt-to-equity ratio of 0.17x, substantial recent operating cash flow of Rs. 86 Cr with strong cash conversion, and a positive institutional money flow [E34, E35, E37, E44].

Conceded: the median return on equity over 10 years is 8% [E26] and the 3-year figure is 11% [E61], but this historical drag is being left behind as current profitability accelerates with a trailing twelve-month profit growth of 30% [E21] and return on capital employed reaching 20% [E10]. The concern over rising borrowings to Rs 56 Cr [E39] ignores the exceptionally conservative debt-to-equity ratio of 0.17x [E37] and the fact that operating cash flow reached a massive Rs 86 Cr with a cash conversion of 2.05x [E34, E35]. While contingent liabilities of Rs 167 Cr exist [E62], they are balanced against strong fundamentals including a sector-beating ROCE of 20% versus the benchmark 10.62% [E10] and positive institutional money flow [E44]. Conceded: operating margins show an inconsistent trend over the last two years [E32, E33], yet the overall operating margin has actually expanded by one percentage point over the TTM period [E30]. Finally, historical volatility and drawdowns [E53, E54] are purely backward-looking metrics that fail to reflect the stellar 96 out of 100 rules-based screen score and strong relative-strength rating of 100 [E51, E64].

Conceded: trailing twelve-month profit growth reached 30% [E21] and cash conversion hit 2.05x with Rs 86 Cr in operating cash flow [E34, E35]. However, dismissing historical returns as a mere past drag is short-sighted when the company's 10-year median return on equity languishes at a meager 8% and the 3-year figure remains low at 11% [E26, E61]. While debt-to-equity sits at a conservative 0.17x [E37], total borrowings have still expanded from Rs 49 Cr to Rs 56 Cr [E39], running parallel to a high cost of borrowing flagged as a negative by the statements [E63]. Furthermore, brushing aside contingent liabilities of Rs 167 Cr [E62] ignores a massive legal and financial overhang that dwarfs the entire free cash flow of Rs 38 Cr [E36]. The claim that operating margins are expanding ignores the official classification that the yearly and quarterly margin trends are inconsistent over the last two years and two quarters [E32, E33]. Finally, treating historical volatility of 56.8% and a devastating peak-to-trough drawdown of -89.8% as irrelevant backward-looking noise [E53, E54] ignores the immense structural downside risk inherent in the equity.

Conceded: the 10-year median return on equity is 8% [E26] and contingent liabilities stand at Rs 167 Cr [E62]. However, the bear's focus on historical returns ignores the clear upward trajectory where recent median ROE has climbed to 13% [E29] and ROCE reaches a robust 20% [E10]. While borrowings increased to Rs 56 Cr [E39], the company maintains a conservative debt-to-equity ratio of just 0.17x [E37] alongside stellar cash conversion of 2.05x generating Rs 86 Cr in operating cash flow [E34, E35]. Conceded: the margin trend is labelled inconsistent [E32, E33], yet operating margins sit higher at 12% in TTM compared to 11% three years prior [E30]. Finally, citing historical drawdown and volatility [E53, E54] ignores the current operational strength, highlighted by a rules-based screen score of 96 out of 100 [E64] and a sector tailwind score of +0.55 [E71].

Conceded: recent median ROE has climbed to 13% [E29] and ROCE reaches a robust 20% [E10]. However, focusing only on these recent figures glosses over the long-term reality of a low 10-year median return on equity of 8% [E26] and a 3-year low return on equity of 11% [E61]. While debt-to-equity is low at 0.17x [E37], borrowings actually grew to Rs 56 Cr from Rs 49 Cr [E39], accompanied by flagged high costs of borrowing [E63] and substantial contingent liabilities of Rs 167 Cr [E62]. Conceded: operating margins sit higher at 12% in TTM compared to three years prior [E30], yet the yearly and quarterly operating margin trends are officially labelled as inconsistent [E32, E33]. Finally, waving away historical volatility and drawdowns ignores a severe 56.8% annualised volatility [E54] and an extreme historical peak-to-trough drawdown of -89.8% [E53].
